course.title: AP U.S. History
course.description: Trace how Americans have argued over identity, power, work, and their place in the world, from the societies that existed before 1491 to the present.
course.previewDescription: Follow the nation's development from early contact and colonization through independence, civil war, industrialization, world wars, and recent decades.

unit.title: Period 4
unit.description: Follow the rise of party politics and a more participatory democracy, the market revolution, westward expansion and foreign policy, the Second Great Awakening and reform, and the growth of slavery from 1800 to 1848.

topics.title: Contextualizing Period 4
topics.summary: The context for Period 4: a more participatory democracy and a new national culture, an economy transformed by innovation, and a nation that expanded westward and argued over slavery, 1800–1848.

topics.title: The Rise of Political Parties and the Era of Jefferson
topics.summary: How the election of 1800, Jefferson's presidency, the Supreme Court's early decisions, and the Louisiana Purchase shaped national politics and the nation's reach across North America.

topics.title: Politics and Regional Interests
topics.summary: How the economic interests of the Northeast, South, and West shaped political positions in the 1810s and 1820s, how the American System aimed to unify the economy, and how the Missouri Compromise postponed the conflict over slavery.

topics.title: America on the World Stage
topics.summary: How the War of 1812, border agreements with Britain and Spain, and the Monroe Doctrine expressed a growing American effort to claim territory, protect trade, and assert influence in the Western Hemisphere.

topics.title: Market Revolution: Industrialization
topics.summary: How entrepreneurs, new machines, and new transportation networks created a market revolution between 1800 and 1848, and why the North, the Midwest, and the South were linked in different ways.

topics.title: Market Revolution: Society and Culture
topics.summary: How the market revolution moved people to cities and to the West, divided Americans into new economic classes, and changed the roles of women and families.

topics.title: Expanding Democracy
topics.summary: How voting expanded from property owners to nearly all adult white men between 1800 and 1848, how party politics changed as a result, and who was left out.

topics.title: Jackson and Federal Power
topics.summary: How Andrew Jackson's presidency divided Democrats and Whigs over the national bank, tariffs, and federal power, and how Indian removal shaped relations with American Indian nations.

topics.title: The Development of an American Culture
topics.summary: How a national culture emerged between 1800 and 1848 from American subjects, European influences, and regional traditions, and how Romantic ideas shaped literature, art, philosophy, and architecture.

topics.title: The Second Great Awakening
topics.summary: Why a wave of Protestant revivals swept the United States after 1800, and how the Second Great Awakening reshaped religion and set the stage for reform.

topics.title: An Age of Reform
topics.summary: How religious revival, voluntary organizations, abolitionism, and the women's rights movement tried to improve American society between 1800 and 1848.

topics.title: African Americans in the Early Republic
topics.summary: How enslaved people resisted and created communities, how free African Americans built institutions and joined antislavery efforts, and what stayed the same and changed in African American life from 1800 to 1848.

topics.title: The Society of the South in the Early Republic
topics.summary: How cotton, soil exhaustion, and the westward movement of slavery shaped the South's economy, society, and sense of regional identity from 1800 to 1848.

topics.title: Causation in Period 4
topics.summary: A guide to explaining the causes and effects of change from 1800 to 1848, and to judging the extent to which politics, economics, and foreign policy promoted an American identity.
